title: RWB-S7-E6017-APP: the routing slice has no plan row for its five consumed contracts, its rule kit, its event library, its meeting calendar, the operation it provides or the requirement it serves
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6017-APP; context pack S7 rwb-writeoff (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 12 and 13); legacy RWB-E6-017; FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 A2.5, A1.4 and Requirements served; TSD S7 Write-off and recovery v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.3, T4, T5.2, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-06, R-WO-10 and R-WO-11; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-24; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-16; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-WOF-05
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S7-E6017-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the step reads the rwb-case case state, answers the case move, assigns the committee queue, reads the deviation on rwb-deviation and reads the WO package on rwb-decision, so five consumed rows have no plan row. (2) DP-04 is absent from the pattern set although the step evaluates the WO route set of 51 rules over 27 states, so no Drools kit row RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is held. (3) DP-09 is absent although the service owns the topic rwb.writeoff.events.v1 and event EV-24 WriteOffApproved, so the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is absent from the H row. (4) DP-10 is absent although the step books the pack into a monthly meeting, and JOB-16, the only job the service owns, is the monthly scan. (5) The two operations the legacy Endpoints table lists are the scan (API-S7-001) and the committee decision (API-S7-002); in the split they belong to RWB-S7-E6013-APP and to RWB-S7-E6018-APP to -E6020-APP, so this step provides no routing operation, and the population read behind SCR-27 has no published path, operation id or element name. (6) No source gives a meeting calendar, a meeting-date column or a Schedule element for the booking, and write_off.committee_date is the committee approval date. (7) write_off.decision_log_id names the P7 decision_log_entry, while DP-03 keeps the record locally, so the column's target meaning is unsettled. (8) The freshness rule VR-S7-005-1 and MSG-P1-001 name v_ace_batch_status, which this service may not read. (9) No requirement row in the plan or in FSD S7 names the routing step.
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S7-E6017-APP: C, I and X empty and reqs empty; context pack S7 ownership rows (one table write_off, two POST operations, one event EV-24, one job JOB-16, one workflow WriteOffWorkflow); TSD S7 T4 rows R-WO-06, R-WO-10 and R-WO-11; FSD S7 A2.5.3.1 VR-S7-005-1 and A2.5.4.4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-06, R-WO-10, R-WO-11 and R-WO-12; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-24 WriteOffApproved published for the write-off and recovery module; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-16 monthly write-off scan
area: Dependency, ownership, interface and requirement trace
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand; record the rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision rows as class C in fact with their placeholders; record RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and a meeting-calendar element as tracked dependencies rather than metadata rows; declare that this step provides no REST operation and that the SCR-27 population read is a placeholder; record the decision_log_id meaning as the local record identifier; land the freshness fact with the pack; and add a requirement row for the routing step at the next programme revision

title: RWB-S7-E6017-CON: the consumed operation names, the queue and deviation elements, the unprinted state values and the meeting-booking element have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6017-CON; context pack S7 rwb-writeoff; legacy RWB-E6-017; FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 A2.5.2, A2.5.3.1, A2.5.3.3 and Screens; TSD S7 Write-off and recovery v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T4, T5.2, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-06, R-WO-10 and R-WO-11; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 /write-off-scans and /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision
description: (1) No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, that assigns a queue item or that routes a case to the deviation handler, so five consumed rows carry placeholders. (2) The queue table of DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008 is named in the legacy Data table but is not this service's and its owner is given only by the case and workflow ownership, so the queue is consumed on the rwb-case contract and its element is not published. (3) The WO rule package read has no published operation name, and DP-04 is not in the pattern set. (4) TSD S7 T4 prints 25 of the 51 rule rows and names the machine as 27 states, so part of the state vocabulary has no printed value. (5) The OpenAPI document of this key declares no routing operation, so the contract declares one read with a placeholder name, the write-off element and the consumed rows, and the population read behind SCR-27 has no published path or operation id. (6) The meeting booking has no column, calendar or Schedule element in any source. (7) write_off.decision_log_id names the P7 decision_log_entry while DP-03 keeps the record locally. (8) TSD S7 T-A.2 gives the error set as status codes with no message id per condition, so each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set.
evidence: TSD S7 T4 ('51 rules over 27 states' and 25 rows printed); TSD S7 T3.1 field list DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020; TSD S7 T-A.1 operations API-S7-001 and API-S7-002 and T-A.2 error lists 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids; legacy RWB-E6-017 Data table entities recovery_case, deviation, queue, decision_log_entry and rule_row and Endpoints table with the two POST rows; FSD S7 Screens SCR-27; API Specification v4 WriteOff element with five required properties
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message id of section 14, declare the case boundary as the child workflow's input, signals and stage outcome, publish the queue and deviation elements with their owners, publish the complete 27-state list, settle the meeting-booking attribute, and confirm the operation names with the rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision owners before the baseline is tagged
